Iteration 16 complete.

**Step 0 — reports backfilled.** Iterations 14 and 15 had results but no post-eval report; both are written (`reports/iteration_14_sibling_units.md`, `reports/iteration_15_formula_coverage.md`), plus the pre-eval design note for this iteration.

**Analysis.** The plateau is noise-dominated — one standard error on the average is ~0.028, so 0.5944 (it 14) and 0.5678 (it 13) are not distinguishable. The evidence that *does* separate is the per-sample flip counts: iteration 14 gained by **deleting** text the check asserted falsely, iteration 15 lost 7 free-form samples to 0 recovered by **adding** prompt text that was true of the corpus (its repair never fired — `repair_turns` is 0 across all 260 samples). Things I measured and rejected before committing: multi-draft consensus (intersection/union both ≤ single-draft on the recorded independent samples), retrieval quality on the free-form corpus (6/30 vs 7/30 random — no lift), and vocabulary visibility on the set-answering corpus (all 134 labels are already in the guide; 28 missed units were visible and still missed).

**The defect found.** `_required_markup` treated *every* bracketed token in the question as output markup. A free-form question states its input as SMILES, which is written in bracket atoms, so the check told the solver "the question asks for `[nH]`, which is missing from the draft" — a false defect under the header the system prompt says to fix. Measured: 9 of 30 val questions and 14 of 50 train ones affected, 12 of 60 recorded samples carrying the false defect, 7 of them correct answers. Also hits the set-answering corpus (2 of 200 train questions cite a year as `[2016]`).

**Change (one method + one constant).** A token is required markup only when the question *uses* it as one: it closes the token (`[X]…[/X]`) or stands within 40 chars of an angle-bracket wrapper (`[X]…<eoa>`). Verified over all 500 questions: the one-unit corpus and set-answering val are byte-identical, 198/200 set-answering train identical, and the 80 free-form questions with invented tags now yield none. Replayed over recorded answers: 260/260 set-answering and one-unit check outputs identical, 48/60 free-form identical, and on the other 12 the only differing line kind is `- Markup:` (12 → 0). 360-call fuzz raises no exception, and true positives survive (a missing `[/DIAGNOSIS]` or `<eoa>` is still reported).

Everything else — memory preparation, retrieval, guide, prompts, skill, middleware — is byte-identical to the best-scoring parent.

CANDIDATES: attested_delimiters
